campaign.name: Youth Camp | Parents
campaign.objective: Help parents of players aged 11 to 15 understand the experience and secure a place at the September youth camp.

concepts.name: They Just Love It
concepts.strategy: Enter through the observable fact that some kids just love basketball. Describe the evidence so the parent recognises their own child. Do not label. Let self-recognition do the work.
concepts.audience: Parents and guardians of basketball players aged 11 to 15 in Birmingham and the West Midlands whose child is enthusiastic about the game.
concepts.proposition: Give their enthusiasm a coached day where they get better, compete and come home buzzing.

ads.primary_text:
Some kids just love basketball.

They are practising around the house. Watching clips. Trying new moves. Asking when training is. You do not have to push them. They would play all day if you let them.

At 11 to 15, that enthusiasm is the thing. The question is not whether they will make it to the top. The question is whether they are in the right environment to grow.

School of Skill Youth Camp. A coached day where they get better, compete and come home buzzing.

27 September 2026. Sandwell Academy, West Bromwich. Ages 11 to 15. £50 per player.

ads.primary_text:
You know the signs.

The ball in their hands walking through the house. The clips they watch on repeat. The question about when the next session is.

They do not need to be convinced. They need a place to get better.

Youth Camp. 27 September 2026. Sandwell Academy. Ages 11 to 15. £50.

concepts.name: The Right Place To Grow
concepts.strategy: Reframe the parent's anxiety from 'is my child going to become elite' to 'my job right now is to give their enthusiasm a good environment'. Surface the parental tension without manufacturing insecurity.
concepts.audience: Parents who want structured basketball development for their child but feel pressure around expectations and outcomes.
concepts.proposition: A coached environment with NBA, England Talent Pathway and professional-level staff where effort and growth matter more than results.

ads.primary_text:
At 11 to 15, they do not need somebody putting huge expectations on them.

They need good coaching, real competition and a place where effort and growth matter more than results.

The rest takes care of itself. Sometimes you simply give something they love the right place to grow.

School of Skill Youth Camp. Coached by former NBA, England Talent Pathway and professional players. All abilities welcome.

27 September 2026. Sandwell Academy, West Bromwich. £50 per player.

ads.primary_text:
You do not have to figure out whether basketball is their future. That is not your job right now.

Your job is to give them a good environment. Coaches who know the game. Players who push them. A place where they can try things, make mistakes and get better.

The Youth Camp is that place.

27 September 2026. Ages 11 to 15. £50.

concepts.name: They Came Home Buzzing
concepts.strategy: Use the existing parent testimonial as a recognition device. The parent recognises the experience through another parent's words. The evidence does the selling.
concepts.audience: Parents considering a basketball camp for their child aged 11 to 15 who want social proof of the experience.
concepts.proposition: A day where they get better, have fun and want more, confirmed by parents who have already sent their child.

ads.primary_text:
"My child came home buzzing, and asking when the next session was."

That is what a parent told us after last year's camp.

Buzzing. Not tired. Not relieved it was over. Asking when the next one was.

That is what happens when a kid spends an afternoon doing something they love, in a place that takes them seriously.

Youth Camp. 27 September 2026. Sandwell Academy, West Bromwich. Ages 11 to 15. £50 per player.
